description: An ORDER BY key may be any in-scope expression, not only a bare column name: a SELECT alias, arithmetic, a parenthesised expression with DESC, or a function call. Three harder cases follow, each of which frostlake once refused with 'ORDER BY expression not found in SELECT list'. After GROUP BY, the key may be a GROUPED COLUMN that is not selected or an AGGREGATE that is not selected (ascending and descending, and with a HAVING in between) - the key is computed over each row's group. And in a WINDOW query, which projects the non-SELECT columns away before ORDER BY runs, an unselected FROM column is still a legal key: it is precomputed during the window projection from the still-available FROM columns, including under QUALIFY, which is the shape the loader emits. Converted 1:1 from query/OrderByExpressionTest (now retired); the Java read the first column of a few rows by index, so each converted test pins the whole ordered row set.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ob (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ob VALUES (3, 1), (1, 10), (2, 3)
SELECT a AS z FROM ob ORDER BY z
CREATE TABLE ob (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ob VALUES (3, 1), (1, 10), (2, 3)
SELECT a, b FROM ob ORDER BY a+b
CREATE TABLE ob (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ob VALUES (3, 1), (1, 10), (2, 3)
SELECT a FROM ob ORDER BY (a*2) DESC
CREATE TABLE ob2 (a INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ob2 VALUES (-3), (1), (-2)
SELECT a FROM ob2 ORDER BY ABS(a)
CREATE TABLE gob (grp INTEGER, k INTEGER)
INSERT INTO gob VALUES (1, 30), (2, 20), (3, 40), (4, 10)
SELECT grp FROM gob GROUP BY grp, k ORDER BY k
CREATE TABLE aob (grp INTEGER, k INTEGER)
INSERT INTO aob VALUES (1, 5), (1, 30), (2, 20), (3, 40)
SELECT grp FROM aob GROUP BY grp ORDER BY MAX(k)
CREATE TABLE dob (grp INTEGER, k INTEGER)
INSERT INTO dob VALUES (1, 5), (1, 30), (2, 20), (3, 40)
SELECT grp FROM dob GROUP BY grp ORDER BY MAX(k) DESC
CREATE TABLE hob (grp INTEGER, k INTEGER)
INSERT INTO hob VALUES (1, 30), (2, 20), (3, 40), (4, 10)
SELECT grp FROM hob GROUP BY grp, k HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1 ORDER BY k
CREATE TABLE wob (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, rid INTEGER)
SELECT a, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY b) rn FROM wob ORDER BY rid
CREATE TABLE qob (cid INTEGER, fid INTEGER, rid INTEGER)
SELECT cid FROM qob QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cid ORDER BY fid DESC) = 1 ORDER BY rid
